decisions.statement: An answer is cast as the change shape the shadow already reads.
A path a move leaves is among the paths the change changed.
The path a move lands at had no body before that move.
An edit stating no body leaves that path with nothing after the change.
A change reads the files and the index through one world.
A world over no answer reads the index committed at the root.
A world over an answer reads the index that answer leaves.
A world has the answer that world was built over.
A world over no answer carries an answer with no edit.
A world built over a second answer has both answers gathered.
A reach answers the world that reach's answer leaves beside that answer.
A reach coming back refused answers the world that reach was handed.
A change reaching more than one change passes each world into the next reach.
A path an answer writes reads back the body that answer leaves at the path.
A path an answer takes away reads back nothing.
A path no answer names reads back the body the world beneath answers.
A world answers the body at a path beside the text at that path.
A world says here whether that world holds text at a path.
A body that is not text is answered as not text rather than as no body.
An answer is replayed over the bodies a world answers rather than over its text.
A world is worked out over the answers gathered so far rather than over one answer.
A world whose shadow will not build throws where the index is asked.
Nothing here builds a second shadow of its own.
A ledger has the edits added so far rather than a world for each answer.
A ledger reads a path from the edits added to that ledger.
A ledger reads a path no edit names from the files beneath.
An index a ledger answers is built again where an edit was added.
A ledger settles the edits added after that ledger last answered an index.
A ledger settles those edits onto the reading that ledger already settled.
A ledger has one memo across every reach rather than one memo for each reach.
A ledger replays those edits onto the bodies that ledger already settled.
A ledger folds the bodies those edits left into the bodies that ledger already settled.
No body an earlier settling already folded in is folded in a second time.
A path the ledger replayed no body for is left out of the settled bodies rather than folded in.
No edit a ledger already settled is settled a second time.
A reach over a ledger adds to that ledger rather than building a second world.
A world a reach answered is passed on rather than built again over that reach's answer.
An answer a change worked out itself is built over as a second world rather than added to a ledger.
A reach that refuses adds nothing to the ledger.
A reach whose edits will not replay comes back refused rather than throwing.
The reason the replay gave is the reason that reach refuses.
An edit that will not replay throws rather than being read as an answer with no edit.
A ledger an edit refused has the edits that ledger had before.
A ledger adds an edit that ledger already added no second time.
An edit is added once by which edit the edit is rather than by the path the edit names.
An edit is read as coming from a path the ledger already left with nothing.
A reach inside a change states an edit the reach around that change states again.
A world answers which folders under a folder are left out beside the paths that folder answers.
Those folders are read from the tree with the answers gathered laid over.
A world says whether a path names a file or a folder in the checkout.
That path is read from the tree with the answers gathered laid over.
Carrying a world onto an answer is one act.
A reach is one caller of that act.
Facing a world as the index reads its properties is one act here rather than one act per change.
A generated body a change writes is carried onto the world and withheld from the answer.
Withholding is done by a reach rather than asked for by each change.
A body carried onto the world rather than answered is formatted as an authored body is.
Which bodies are generated is read through the face built before the change rather than after it.
A face reads the index when that face is asked rather than when that face is built.
A face reads the files through the world rather than through the checkout.
The face a world is read through is built once for that world.
A reach whose answer could turn the generated bodies builds that face again.
An answer stating anything but a replace could turn the generated bodies.
A replace on a page type or on a page property could turn the generated bodies.
A replace leaving a page stating a second page type could turn those bodies.
The page type a body states is read from `type`, and from `pageTypeSlug` after.
That page type is read from the body before and after rather than from the passage carried.
A replace carries the passage that turned rather than the body around it.
A replace leaving a page stating the page type it stated turns no such body.
Every other replace reads the face already built.
A reach withholding a body works on a ledger.

definition: the files and index as the answer a change gives would leave both
